title: The Brain-Wiring Test
introduction: This test is designed to indicate the masculinity or femininity of your brain patterns. There are no right or wrong answers – the result is simply an indication of the probable level of male hormone your brain did, or did not, receive around six to eight weeks after your conception. This is reflected in your preference of values, behaviours, style, orientations and choices.
instructions: Circle the statement that is most likely to be true for you most of the time.

questions.question: When it comes to reading a map or street directory you:

options.a: have difficulty and often ask for help
options.b: turn it round to face the direction you're going
options.c: have no difficulty reading maps or street directories

questions.question: You're cooking a complicated meal with the radio playing and a friend phones. Do you:

options.a: leave the radio on and continue cooking while talking on the phone
options.b: turn the radio off, talk and keep cooking
options.c: say you'll call them back as soon as you've finished cooking

questions.question: Friends are coming to visit and ask for directions to your new house. Do you:

options.a: draw a map with clear directions and send it to them or get someone else to explain how to get there
options.b: ask what landmarks they know then try to explain to them how to get there
options.c: explain verbally how to get there: 'Take the M3 to Newcastle, turn off, turn left, go to the second traffic lights ...'

questions.question: When explaining an idea or concept, are you more likely to:

options.a: use a pencil, paper and body language gestures
options.b: explain it verbally using body language and gestures
options.c: explain it verbally, being clear and concise

questions.question: When coming home from a great movie, you prefer to:

options.a: picture scenes from the movie in your mind
options.b: talk about the scenes and what was said
options.c: quote mainly what was said in the movie

questions.question: In a cinema, you usually prefer to sit:

options.a: on the right side
options.b: anywhere
options.c: on the left side

questions.question: A friend has something mechanical that won't work. You would:

options.a: sympathise, and discuss how they feel about it
options.b: recommend someone reliable who can fix it
options.c: figure out how it works and attempt to fix it for them

questions.question: You're in an unfamiliar place and someone asks you where North is. You:

options.a: confess you don't know
options.b: guess where it is, after a bit of thought
options.c: point towards North without difficulty

questions.question: You've found a parking space but it's tight and you must reverse into it. You would:

options.a: rather try to find another space
options.b: carefully attempt to back into it
options.c: reverse into it without any difficulty

questions.question: You are watching TV when the telephone rings. You would:

options.a: answer the phone with the TV on
options.b: turn the TV down and then answer
options.c: turn the TV off, tell others to be quiet and then answer

questions.question: You've just heard a new song by your favourite artist. Usually you:

options.a: can sing some of the song afterwards without difficulty
options.b: can sing some of it afterwards if it's a really simple song
options.c: find it hard to remember how the song sounded but you might recall some of the words

questions.question: You are best at predicting outcomes by:

options.a: using intuition
options.b: making a decision based on both the available information and 'gut feeling'
options.c: using facts, statistics and data

questions.question: You've misplaced your keys. Would you:

options.a: do something else until the answer comes to you
options.b: do something else, but keep trying to remember where you put them
options.c: mentally retrace your steps until you remember where you left them

questions.question: You're in a hotel room and you hear the distant sound of a siren. You:

options.a: couldn't identify where it's coming from
options.b: could probably point to it if you concentrate
options.c: could point straight to where it's coming from

questions.question: You go to a social meeting and are introduced to seven or eight new people. Next day you:

options.a: can easily picture their faces
options.b: would remember a few of their faces
options.c: would be more likely to remember their names

questions.question: You want to go to the country for your holiday but your partner wants to go to a beach resort. To convince them your idea is better, you:

options.a: tell them sweetly how you feel: you love the countryside and the kids and family always have fun there
options.b: tell them if they go to the country you'll be grateful and will be happy to go to the beach next time
options.c: use the facts: the country resort is closer, cheaper, and well-organised for sporting and leisure activities

questions.question: When planning your day's activities, you usually:

options.a: write a list so you can see what needs to be done
options.b: think of the things you need to do
options.c: picture in your mind the people you will see, places you will visit and things you'll be doing

questions.question: A friend has a personal problem and has come to discuss it with you. You:

options.a: are sympathetic and understanding
options.b: say that problems are never as bad as they seem and explain why
options.c: give suggestions or rational advice on how to solve the problem

questions.question: Two friends from different marriages are having a secret affair. How likely are you to spot it?

options.a: you could spot it very early
options.b: you'd pick up on it half the time
options.c: you'd probably miss it

questions.question: What is life all about, as you see it?

options.a: having friends and living in harmony with those around you
options.b: being friendly to others while maintaining personal independence
options.c: achieving worthwhile goals, earning others' respect and winning prestige and advancement

questions.question: Given the choice, you would prefer to work:

options.a: in a team where people are compatible
options.b: around others but maintaining your own space
options.c: by yourself

questions.question: The books you prefer to read are:

options.a: novels and fiction
options.b: magazines and newspapers
options.c: non-fiction, autobiographies

questions.question: When you go shopping you tend to:

options.a: often buy on impulse, particularly the specials
options.b: have a general plan but take it as it comes
options.c: read the labels and compare costs

questions.question: You prefer to go to bed, wake up and eat meals:

options.a: whenever you feel like it
options.b: on a basic schedule but you are flexible
options.c: at about the same time each day

questions.question: You've started a new job and met lots of new people on the staff. One of them phones you when you are at home. You would:

options.a: find it easy to recognise their voice
options.b: recognise it about half the time
options.c: have difficulty identifying the voice

questions.question: What upsets you most when arguing with someone?

options.a: their silence or lack of response
options.b: when they won't see your point of view
options.c: their probing or challenging questions and comments

questions.question: In school how did you feel about spelling tests and writing essays?

options.a: you found them both fairly easy
options.b: you were generally OK with one but not the other
options.c: you weren't very good at either

questions.question: When it comes to dancing or jazz routines, you:

options.a: can 'feel' the music once you've learnt the steps
options.b: can do some exercises or dances, but get lost with others
options.c: have difficulty keeping time or rhythm

questions.question: How good are you at identifying and mimicking animal sounds?

options.a: not very good
options.b: reasonable
options.c: very good

questions.question: At the end of a long day, you usually prefer to:

options.a: talk to friends or family about your day
options.b: listen to others talk about their day
options.c: read a paper, watch TV and not talk

scoring.description: First, add the number of A, B and C responses and use the following table to arrive at your final result.
scoring.note: For any questions where the answers didn't accurately reflect your life or you left them blank, award yourself five points.

analysis:
Most males will score between 0–180 and most females 150–300. Brains that are 'wired' for mainly masculine thinking usually score below 150. The closer to 0 they are, the more masculine they are, and the higher their testosterone level is likely to be. These people demonstrate strong logical, analytical and verbal skills and tend to be disciplined and well-organised. The closer to 0 they score, the better they are at projecting costs and planning outcomes for statistical data, with their emotions hardly influencing them at all.

Scores in the minus range are high masculine scores. These scores show that large amounts of testosterone were present in the early stages of foetal development. The lower the score for a woman, the more likely she will be to have lesbian tendencies.

Brains that are wired for mainly feminine thinking will score higher than 180. The higher the number, the more feminine the brain will be, and the more likely the person is to demonstrate significant creative, artistic and musical talents. They will make more of their decisions on intuition or gut feeling, and are good at recognising problems using minimal data. They are also good at solving problems using creativity and insight. The higher the score is above 180 for a man, the greater the chance he will be gay.

Males who score below 0 and women who score above 300 have brains that are wired so oppositely that the only thing they are likely to have in common is that they live on the same planet!

Scores between 150–180 show compatibility of thought for both sexes, or a foot in both sexual camps. These people do not show a bias for either male or female thinking and usually demonstrate a flexibility in thinking that can be a significant advantage to any group who are going through a problem-solving process. They have the predisposition to make friends with both men and women.
